articleTitle: Challenges in Reliable Power System Planning and Management with Large Scale Infusion of Renewable Sources in India
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: India has been continuously thriving to augment its renewable energy base to 175 GW across the overall energy spectrum from currently installed capacity of 60.17 MW by 2022, with 100 GW of solar, 60 GW of wind, 10 GW of bioenergy and 5 GW of small hydro. Since India is getting transformed from a power deficit nation to a power surplus nation, it needs to thoroughly look into how major portion of these inherently unpredictable (or non-dispatch able) sources can be integrated into the electric system without compromising stability, safe operations and security of grid. This paper discusses the challenges involved in planning and management of Indian power system which is currently dominated by conventional energy sources, with large scale infusion of renewable sources which is currently dominated by conventional energy sources. This paper also suggests possible solutions for managing the variability of these non-dispatch able renewable sources.

articleTitle: A Statistical Approach for Condition Evaluation and Residual Lifetime Estimation of MV Power Cables
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The general idea of preventive maintenance approach allowed most of the asset managers of power utilities to understand that a condition based maintenance approach is the only way to recognize aging effects and weak points, replace the weak cable sections and finally guarantee a distribution cable network condition with high reliability. This paper describes the new approach of statistical estimation of the remaining life time of power cables that allows operating underground cables to the operational limit.

articleTitle: Cooperative Control for Distributed Energy Storage Systems with Different Droop Schemes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Different types of power grids have different characteristics which require proper control methods to be implemented. Typically, droop control schemes are utilized at the primary control level due to their simplicity and quick response. Nevertheless, those droop methods can be varied depending on the power grid impedance, and hence, various secondary control protocols might be needed. This research proposes a distributed design approach for distributed battery energy storage systems (BESSs) at the higher control level corresponding to three different droop schemes implemented at the lower control level for various grid conditions. The designed controllers use multi-agent system and consensus theory to regulate the voltage/frequency and synchronize the energy level as well as active and reactive power sharing among BESSs. A modified IEEE 57-bus power system is used in the simulation for validation purpose.

articleTitle: Improved Distribution System Overcurrent Protection using Tolerance-based Time-current Coordination
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The availability of information on the accuracy of current sensing, relaying and protective device operation, along with the high accuracy sensing precision, and fast clearing times achieved by certain modern distribution protection devices, enable improved distribution overcurrent protection using tolerance-based time-current coordination rather than following the existing convention of using a specified coordinating time interval (CTI) or grading interval. This paper discusses the significant differences in tolerance-based time-current coordination performance between existing and certain modern protective devices and presents the methodology used to achieve improved overcurrent protection using multiple series protective devices on a distribution feeder.

articleTitle: The Value of Prosumers’ Flexibility under Different Electricity Market Conditions: Case Studies of Denmark and Croatia
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: To reduce greenhouse gas emissions, power system strategies have focused on large scale integration of renewable energy sources (RES) subsidizing initial installations for a fixed time period to ensure investment profitability. However, increasing number of wind and solar (PV) power plants, not responsible for scheduling deviations due to their intermittent production, resulted in growing need for power system flexibility. By rescinding incentives and subsidies and exposing RES to the market, they become responsible for accurate prediction of their production and become penalized for deviations from the announced forecasts.Moreover, the suppliers, or the aggregators, will play an important role in unlocking and encouraging the flexible end-consumers with installed local RES and demand response (DR). They need to create market products in a form of different dynamic pricing schemes which award responsiveness to price signals and penalize passive behavior.The paper focuses on the value of household flexibility through electricity cost reduction in low and high developed energy power markets. Results show that households equipped with PV and different types of DR programs in high-liquid market (as one in Denmark), exposed to the volatile market prices and responsible for their PV production and demand forecast, achieve lower electricity cost comparing to poorly developed retail market in Croatia where consumers are better off in a two-price tariff system.

articleTitle: Power Voltage Transformers for Renewable Energy Substations Auxiliary Services Supply
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Power Voltage Transformers (PVT) also known as Station Service Voltage Transformers (SSVT) are used to supply Low Voltage power directly from a High Voltage line up to 550kV. Located within the own substation they can provide power up to 333kVA per phase in a reliable and cost-effective way. They offer a wide range of applications, but they excel when substation auxiliary service power supply is needed in remote areas, making them an ideal solution for Renewable Energy substations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic and Electromechanical Transient Hybrid Simulation of Grid-connected Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The large-scale utilization of clean energy represented by photovoltaic(PV) is an inevitable trend of future energy development. To analyze the impact of grid-connected PV on transient characteristics of power grid, this paper first establishes the electromagnetic transient simulation model of PV system. Then the electromagnetic and electromechanical transient hybrid simulation model of grid-connected PV system is established on Matlab/Simulink and PSCAD platform. The key problems of hybrid simulation such as equivalence of electromagnetic side and electromechanical side, interface processing and simulation timing are described. Finally, the correctness of the hybrid simulation algorithm is verified in a simple two-machine system. The algorithm proposed in this paper can be extended to other types of distributed generations, which provides a theoretical basis and platform for the simulation of multi-type distributed generations access to the grid.

articleTitle: An Interval Unit Commitment with Wind Power Integrated Using Interval Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Unit commitment is important in economy and security of power system operation. However, Large penetration of wind power integrated into power system increases the uncertainty on unit commitment. How to efficiently accommodate the uncertainty has been researched widely. In this paper, a new interval unit commitment (UC) formulation based on interval optimization is proposed in which the uncertain wind power is described as fluctuant intervals. Then, the interval UC with uncertainty is transformed into a deterministic form by using order relation of interval number and degree of satisfaction. The transformed model is a two-stage and multi-objective optimization problem. Therefore, the intergeneration projection genetic algorithm is developed to deal with the transformed deterministic model. Finally, the case study with IEEE 39-bus system demonstrated the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Flexibility and Frequency Security Enhancement to Generation Expansion Planning Framework
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The traditional generation expansion planning (GEP) framework focuses on system adequacy where generation portfolio can cover the growing peak demand, taking into account the uncertainty. The need for low-carbon society, makes renewable portfolio (solar, wind, hydro, biomass, etc.) grow rapidly in many countries. Unfortunately, variable renewables (VR), i.e. wind, solar and small hydro, are changing conventional power system planning philosophy. On one side, dispatch characteristics require high flexible capacities to respond with the changes of system net load. The other side is that, frequency dynamics may deteriorate because the conventional generation is replaced by near-zero inertia generation and non-governor control. To encounter these problems, this study enhances flexibility and frequency security assessment into traditional GEP framework. The proposed framework is demonstrated on the modified IEEE RTS-1996, considering only high penetration of solar photovoltaics. Furthermore, simulation results signify that the optimal plan satisfies both flexibility and frequency security point of view.

articleTitle: H∞ Robust Control Design for a Combined Cycle Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: In this paper, a H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> robust controller is designed and implemented for a combined cycle power plant (CCPP). The proposed approach is designed for the speed and temperature control loops. It aims at improving CCPP output responses in the presence of load demand variations and frequency drops. The design procedure entails first estimating and validating a linear auto regressive with exogenous input (ARX) model for the power plant, then synthesizing a H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> robust controller to guarantee the robust stability and performance of the combined cycle power plant in the presence of sudden changes in electric load demands, frequency fluctuations, and uncertainties. The effectiveness of proposed control design is assessed using the nonlinear model of the CCPP and further compared to that of a conventional PID-based CCPP controller. The obtained results showed that implementing an advanced multivariable H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> control approach can improve the response and control accuracy of a CCPP.

articleTitle: Practical Test of Contactless Rotational Piezoelectric Generator for Low Speed Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Piezoelectric has drawn significant attention as the smart and straightforward generator as energy harvester for decades. The principle of this theology is to transform the vibration from itself blending become electricity through the piezoelectric effect phenomenal. Piezoelectric has been used to generate electricity through the cantilever form. However, it still hard to apply with the rotational movement. This research represents the practical optimization test of the rotational piezoelectric generator for a low-speed application such as application in ocean wave or wearable device under the speed between 10 to 100 RPM. The design was applied a pushing force of two permanent magnets which, attached at the far end of the piezoelectric cantilever in stator and the rotational disk in rotor. When the application load drives the rotor, the magnetic field from each permanent magnet will repulse each other and generate AC electricity. The experimental result shows the possibility to harvest energy in the range of 5.92 and 234.47 microwatts at 10 RPM (0.167 Hz) and 100 RPM (1.667 Hz) in order.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Constrained Optimal Power Flow by Particle Swarm Optimization with Time Varying Acceleration Coefficients
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This article presents a technique to solve an optimal power flow problem taking into account transient stability constraint with the objective to minimize the system total generation cost subject to system and individual generating unit constraints. The developed algorithm was based on particle swarm optimization with time varying acceleration coefficients (PSO-TVAC) to determine an optimal output of generating units that offers both economy and security to the system. The developed PSO-based methodology for TSCOPF was tested on the IEEE 30-bus system. The simulation results show that the PSO-TVAC is capable of locating high quality solutions to the problem.

articleTitle: Online Tuning of Power System Stabilizer using Synchrophasor Data
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper discusses an approach for online tuning of Power System Stabilizer (PSS) using synchrophasor measurements. The methodology uses the data obtained from local phasor measurement unit installed at the generator bus to estimate the modes of oscillations and subsequently determines the parameters of the PSS to damp the critical modes. The well known residue based method is used to tune the PSS and the mode estimation is done using the ESPRIT method. The entire scheme is tested and validated on Real Time Digital Simulator. WSCC 9 bus system is used for the simulation study.

articleTitle: Future Approach and Advantages of IEC 61850 Implemented for EGAT Digital Substation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Realizing the importance and the advantages of a new standard for communication, Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand (EGAT), which is a state enterprise responsible for electric power generation and transmission, implements IEC 61850 at the Chatuchak (CTC) substation as a pilot project. This paper presents the EGAT's project of a digital substation which is expectedly planned to be as a standard in technical documents for the bidding process in the year 2019. The structure of IEC 61850 and the EGAT's relaying diagram on which the Bay level is completely dedicated for digital communication are illustrated here. The practical cases of time saving and cost reducing affected from changing to a digital substation are also discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis on Market Mechanism of Demand Response and its Outlook in China
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Demand response (DR) is a change in the power consumption of an electric customer, either reducing or suspending electricity load at a certain period of time to better match power supply. In China, the implementation of DR is so far mainly led by government and has not play a role in power system operation yet, due to lack of corresponding market mechanism. Subsidies for users have funding concern, and bring risks to the sustainability of DR. In this paper, the construction suggestion of market mechanism of DR in China is proposed. The paper summarizes the US and European DR experience first. Then it introduces the key DR pilot projects in China. Finally the paper presents the suggestion and outlook of DR mechanism in the Chinese electricity market.

articleTitle: Assessment of Voltage Sag and Temporary Overvoltage for Neutral Grounding Resistance in Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper presents the impact of neutral resistor grounding of a power transformer on voltage sag and temporary overvoltage (TOV) caused by single line to ground (SLG) faults. The simulations were carried out on a modified 22kV distribution system of provincial electricity authority (PEA). It can be obtained from the study results that the installation of neutral grounding resistors (NGR) has an advantage in reducing voltage sag but has a disadvantage in introducing TOV. While the cost of voltage sag is reduced, TOV can be so significant that it can damage surge arresters installed at distribution transformers and therefore replacing surge arresters with ones having a higher voltage rating is required. A sensitivity analysis was carried out by varying the ohmic value of NGR. The study results are useful to determine the proper NGR that can offers a compromise solution between cost of voltage sag and cost of equipment replacement.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of Distribution Transformer in PEA using CBRM
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Normally, the maintenance of the transformers of distribution systems mainly use time-based maintenance (TBM) because they are easy to manage. However, the cost of operation by such maintenance is high and it does not completely solve the problem of defective equipment. In addition, the maximum performance of distribution transformers may be influenced by the results of such maintenance. To solve the above mentioned problems, this paper presents the conditional-based risk management (CBRM) used in the maintenance planning of transformer distribution systems. There are many conditions for selecting the CBRM process. The health index (HI) is used in the processing to evaluate the importance of management planning. The results of HI are evaluated by weighting score method. The weighting scores depend on the importance of variables, such as transformer life, number of customers, load characteristics, and transformer rating, etc. As a result, the distribution plan can be effectively defined. The proposed method can reduce maintenance costs and reduce the potential risk in the distribution system. Moreover, the Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA) can make use of human resources and assets of the organization more efficiently.

articleTitle: Field Diagnosis on Transformers for Wind Turbine Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Distribution transformers used in wind turbine applications are exposed to additional stress caused by permanent mechanical vibrations, strong load cycling and harsh climatic conditions. These influences can cause an accelerated ageing of the insulation system and shortening of the life expectancy of these essential components of wind power stations. To avoid spontaneous failure of the transformer, regular on site diagnosis contributes to an increased reliability of the whole power system by early detection of the degradation of the insulation system. An induced voltage test with partial discharge measurement is the most significant and productive method for the assessment of the dielectric condition. The most efficient way with respect to availability and logistics is to perform the induced voltage test on-site. Because of the very limited space inside the wind power systems, specialized test equipment was developed for the regular on-site inspection. This compact test voltage source is based on a small IGBT inverter with filter and step-up transformer. It comprises a state of the art control computer to enable a closed loop control of the test voltage. The test voltage source is divided into three small transport units (boxes) and can be used directly in the nacelle. First field tests in 2017 proved the suitability of the compact test voltage source to perform induced voltage tests with accompanying partial discharge measurement. Such field tests were executed continuously throughout the last years and it could be proven that the test system could be integrated into the different service regimes. The test system is suitable for the on-site diagnosis of any kind of cast-resin and distribution transformer too.

articleTitle: Distributed Optimal Operation for Distribution Networks with Multi-microgrid Based on ADMM
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: In recent years, with the development and application of distributed generation, multi-microgrid structure has gradually become a future development form. However, new challenges have been brought to optimal operation due to its structural dispersion, complex composition, and information barrier. This paper proposes a distributed optimal operation model and solution method based on alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. The original problem is decoupled into several independent sub-problems including distribution network and microgrids. Based on the second-order cone relaxed power flow model and the chance-constrained method, the model is optimized to realize the optimal operation of a distribution network with multi-microgrid. Finally, a case study is presented based on the modified IEEE33 node system, and the result illustrates the feasibility of the ADMM algorithm and it is applicable to optimize the operation of distribution networks with multi-microgrid.

articleTitle: Diagnostic Measurement Practices for Instrument Transformers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Statistical study indicates that around 95% of Instrument Transformer failures are not maintenance related but are result of either causes introduced before putting into service or due to incorrect operation. To design a suitable maintenance plan for Instrument Transformers (IT), it is very important to understand their most prominent failure modes, identify the testing tools available and to find a perfect fit to suit the requirements within the limitation of site conditions. In this paper the different failure modes of IT are analyzed. Further the different diagnostic practices, along with their suitability and interpretation are discussed to aid the user to make an informed decision for condition-based maintenance.

articleTitle: Hybrid Control Method Applied on Grid Connected 3-phase Boost Inverter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The utilization of renewable energy sources nowadays is increasing rapidly due to the cheaper price of the photovoltaic cells, wind turbines or other renewable sources. But as a system, these sources usually require power converters either to provide the correct voltage to electric loads or to provide the required currents as in the grid connected application. Many converter topologies are developed for the grid connected applications and one of the topologies is the 3-phase boost inverter. This converter topology, although has a uni-directional power flow, allows the low dc to high ac voltage direct conversion, thus the amount of the power switches is minimum. The particularity of this topology is its non-linearity, where applying the linear control is somewhat more difficult. In this research, a hybrid control approach is proposed to this topology, the 3-phase converter is grid-connected and the whole system is simulated using the PSIM software.

articleTitle: Start-up and Shut-down Control Scheme of DC Distribution Network based on Star Topology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The DC distribution network based on the star topology belongs to a centralized control structure, which has the advantages of easy control and management, easy fault diagnosis and isolation, small delay time, and low transmission error. In this paper, the star topology of DC distribution network is analyzed firstly. Secondly, the start-up and shut-down control scheme of DC distribution network based on star topology are designed. Finally, the above control scheme is verified by real time digital simulator (RTDS) platform. Simulation results show that the control scheme can achieve smooth start-up and shut-down control of the DC distribution network.

articleTitle: An Incremental ELM Method for Hourly Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Electrical load is affected by multiple factors. Machine learning has the ability to approximate complicate nonlinear relations, thus its application in load forecasting has received much attention. However, common machine learning technologies put high requirement for data consistency. Load varies periodically and non-periodically over time, to cover the influence factors is obvious unrealistic. To solve this problem, a load forecasting model based on ensemble learning is proposed. In this framework, knowledge is updated continuously to keep track with the latest data distribution. Information entropy is applied to measure the changes in data distribution. The evolutionary process is done through genetic algorithm. Considering the randomness of sub-model, extreme learning machine (ELM) is adopted. In the end, this method is verified through ISO-New England actual load data.

articleTitle: Techno-economic Feasibility Assessment of Implementation of Solar Tracking for Utility Scale Solar Photovoltaic Plants in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)

authors.preferredName: E. M. S. D De Seram

abstract: Solar tracking is a method for enhancing the energy yield of a solar photovoltaic array by orienting the solar panels to align with the path of the sun using an electro mechanical drive system. The details of different tracking systems, their performances and their extra yields tend to exhibit high variances strongly depending on the location where it is implemented. Based on this, there is an argument that there is no significant requirement for implementing solar tracking for solar parks in equatorial regions like Sri Lanka, that experience a good solar irradiance throughout all months of the year. The paper presents the results of a techno-economic feasibility analysis of implementing solar tracking, carried out for a utility scale solar photovoltaic plant of a selected site location in Sri Lanka. During the analysis, the energy yields of different tracking systems were estimated by incorporating the weather data for the selected site location. The results obtained were incorporated with a sound cost benefit analysis to justify the techno economic feasibility of solar tracking strategy for Sri Lankan context.The paper also contains some proposals for future directions for improving tracking systems to enhance their ability to harness more solar energy.

articleTitle: Finite Element Modeling of 400 kV ERS Bypass Transmission Line Quantifying Installation Difficulty
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Economics of the power system infrastructure is critically dependent on the reliable transmission network. Steel make emergency restoration structure was designed and developed for emergency by-pass of the 400 kV line tower damaged by severe weather condition and soil erosion at the river bed. The emergency restoration system (ERS) was developed to have a wider base arrangement to absorb and distribute the loads on the sandy land of a dried river bed. Finite element analysis (FEA) was conducted on Catia V5R20 to analyze the load on the tower due to weather and estimate the numbers of guyed and maximum angle for the tower. Moreover, 32 numbers of guyed wire required to support the tower at height of 36 m to counter the transverse and lateral load for the span of 475 m and 275 m ensuring safety and electrical clearances to avoid line trip. Site challenges of the continuous stream to erode the base of the tower and raising water level have been discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Correlation Analysis between Quantified Uncertainty Factors and Optimal Operation Cost of Commercial Building-distributed Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: In this study, uncertainties arising from distributed energy resources (DER) of a commercial building is quantified, and the relationship is analyzed between optimal DER operating costs and the variation of uncertainties. Firstly, an optimization algorithm for DER management of a commercial building is introduced. A photovoltaic (PV) generation with energy storage system (ESS) is utilized to reduce peak load consumed by the building and to contribute surplus energy to the electricity grid system. Demand response (DR) issuance is assumed from the given historical data. An electric vehicle (EV) charging station is applied to the DER system which can exchange charging and discharging power with the grid system. Furthermore, uncertainties are quantified based on the distributed resource characteristics. It is inserted in the process of determining the optimal solution and is used as an indicator of the correlation with the minimum operating cost result. Finally, a criterion is proposed to ensure sufficient predictive accuracy of resources that contain randomness for meaningful optimal operation.

articleTitle: Minimized Financial Losses Due to Interruptions and Voltage Sags with Consideration of Investment Cost
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of minimized financial losses due to interruptions and voltage sags with consideration of investment cost. The Modified RBTS Bus 2 test system was used for simulations and Information Technology Industry Council (ITIC) curve was assumed to be a voltage tolerance curve for sensitive industrial customers. Two types of lines were considered: overhead lines and underground cables. Monte-Carlo simulations were used to simulate faults on lines in the Modified RBTS Bus 2 test system. Numbers of unacceptable interruptions and voltage sags were estimated from fault simulations. Results showed that changing certain overhead lines to underground cables can yield minimized financial losses due to interruptions and voltage sags with consideration of investment cost.

articleTitle: Robust Control of Wind Turbines under Uncertain Wind Speed Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Wind speed uncertainty is a huge challenge in wind energy conversion (WEC) systems especially for utility-scale wind turbines. As the wind turbine sizes continue to grow, advanced control strategies have become essential for a reliable and profitable wind power generation. This paper proposes a control approach where wind speed uncertainty is explicitly taken into account for a guaranteed stability and adequate tracking performance of a Doubly Fed Induction Generator Wind Turbine (DFIG - WT). The proposed design is based on the wind speed measurements that are corrupted with uncertainties. A Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI)-based robust controller is proposed where the uncertainty is modeled in polytopic sets. The control performances are assessed subject to two wind profiles i.e. step and real-pattern wind speed. Comparative studies are carried out against a classical PI based controller. The results indicate that the robust controller has inherently ensured the system stability even with the presence of uncertainty while simultaneously ensuring adequate tracking performance. Meanwhile, the PI controller even though great in tracking but cannot guarantee the system stability due to the uncertainty.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study and Evaluation between Fired Domestic Coal Subcritical and Mixed Import Coal Super-critical Power Units in Viet Nam: The Economic-Technical Terms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: In recent years the coal-fired power plants in Viet Nam have applied many solutions to limit environmental pollutions as electrostatic precipitators operated under oil and/or co-fuel firing condition, and especially the first supercritical unit has been operating commercially for decades under sub-critical technology. To speed up applied ultra super-critical technology which may increase the efficiency and decrease carbon dioxide emission, an experimental study and evaluation between fired domestic coal sub-critical and mixed import coal super-critical units was carried out. The study and evaluation focus on plant net heat rate, plant net efficiency, net standard coal consumption rate, and carbon dioxide emission rate - which are calculated based on mass and energy balance method at 100% and 75% rate output. In addition, the proposed amount of liquidated damages for performance guarantees is also determined. From the results of this study, the authors suggest that the performance guarantees and tests of new units should be carried out at all stable loads including minimum load with coal firing.

articleTitle: Asset Performance Enhancement Initiatives on Major Switchgears and Transformers in CLP Power Hong Kong
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: CLP Power Hong Kong Limited (CLP Power), as one of Asia's leading power companies, is at the forefront of implementing new technology to transform its conventional power grid into a smart grid to enhance the grid performance and to support the vision for Hong Kong as a leading smart city of the future. Driven by increasing maturity of digitalisation and technological innovation to the methodologies of equipment condition monitoring system, CLP Power grasped the opportunity in rendering optimisation of the maintenance strategies. Implementation of structured Condition-Based Maintenance (CBM) is an initiative of CLP Power to enhance the asset performance in the power system, with transmission transformers, reactors and switchgears. One of the critical success factors for CBM is having a sound decision support system in place. The condition of the individual equipment can be assessed with the aid of condition monitoring facilities collecting the operating and health data by on-line and off-line means. This paper shares CLP Power's experience in application of condition monitoring technologies with associated decision support system in transmission and distribution power grid asset management to ensure a cost effective and reliable energy supply to enhance the performance of major switchgears and transformers.

Author Keywords: Multi-gas On-line Dissolved Gas Analysis (MODGA) system

articleTitle: Driving Reliability with Machine Learning and Improving Operation by Digitalization of Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: For the new challenges of energy supply a new generation of analytical capabilities with the ability to provide deeper insights is mandatory. Machine learning in combination with artificial intelligence can become the new methodological approach for the diagnostics of equipment in the distribution network. In that way machine learning is based on pattern and evaluation of statistical values and herewith it generates knowledge from experience. The decision-making process is often impaired by unplanned outages. In order to efficiently operate and maintain existing systems and prevent critical failures on power transformers, the right monitoring and control system must be present. This paper introduces also an advanced method for analysis, visualization and interpretation of vibroacoustic of online measurements of on-load tap-changers, particularly in relation to their application with transformers in service.

articleTitle: Underground Cable Fault Location via Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: In recent years, Metropolitan Electricity Authority (MEA) has increasingly replaced the overhead lines with underground cables in Bangkok Metropolitan Area. This is to improve the efficiency and reliability of the distribution system, and also the esthetic quality of the landscape. However, the processes of locating and repairing underground cable faults are generally more difficult and time-consuming than those for overhead lines. This article proposed the use of Random Forest algorithm to locate faults for medium voltage underground cables. When tested on the MEA's open-loop underground cable system, this algorithm was capable of finding the fault locations with high accuracy, and can serve system operators and crew staff as a guideline for an efficient system service restoration.

articleTitle: Impact of Variable Energy Resources on Energy Imbalance Markets and Wheeling Transactions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Increased installation of renewable variable generation causes unpredictable flow patterns. Traditionally, Path Operation Limits (SOL) are computed using cases with well-adjusted voltage levels and with reactive devices set to ensure that system studies show acceptable post-contingency performance. When Variable Energy Resources produce frequent, large variations in power transfer, the actual operating conditions can be significantly different than what was assumed when calculating the SOL. This leaves the system at risk of unacceptable dynamic or post-transient response to critical contingencies. The Variable Transfer Limit (VTL) is the amount of frequent variability in power transfer that can be accommodated while ensuring reliable system operation. This paper presents a novel method to compute VTL calculations. An approach is also presented to compute the VTL vs SOL nomogram using the node/breaker model State Estimator (SE) cases. The presented approach is used to compute path VTLs in the Northwest. The VTL can be used for Energy Imbalance Markets, wheeling transactions and remote balancing. The computed VTL limits are used in California ISO (CAISO) EIM market and an implementation approach is presented.

articleTitle: Controller Hardware-in-the-loop Implementation for Agent-based Distributed Optimal Power Flow Using ADMM on Cyber-Physical Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper presents the optimal power flow (OPF) implementation in the distributed manner of a cyber-physical connected microgrid. A laboratory testbed is introduced for the deployment including digital real-time simulator OPAL-RT, a cluster of Raspberry PIs (RPIs) and a local communication network. The general OPF problem is formulated and separated into bus-based subsystems. Agent is run on each RPI to implement alternating direction method of multiplier (ADMM) to solve OPF based on local information and adjacent data, then send power set points to physical system on OPAL-RT. The experiment on a 6-bus microgrid test case shows that the system operates at the optimal state under the control of the cyber system.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Behavior of the 3rd Harmonic over Power Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Due to a large use of power electronics devices, the power grid has experienced increasing harmonic pollution that has started to interfere in the performance of power transmission lines. For correctly evaluating how this interference can be, analytical modelling of transmission lines can play a very important role for serving as an alternative to computer tools. This is what is shown in this work for the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> power harmonic, based on a methodology developed by the authors that have already proofed as being satisfactory for the power frequency and for the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> power harmonic. For better illustrating the application of the developed methodology, some key representative cases are presented as happening in a practical 230 kV power transmission line.

articleTitle: Optimal Capacity Design for Solar-assisted CCHP System Integrated with Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: In this paper, a new system of solar-assisted combined cooling heating and power (CCHP) system equipped with energy storage is proposed. The model consists of most of the equipment which may be used in the distributed energy system, especially the concentrating solar power (CSP) plant which can store the solar power absorbed into large-capacity thermal storage device. Other energy storage devices are also taken into consideration in this system so as to store the surplus energy. Then a two-level optimization strategy for capacity design, which employs the group search optimizer (GSO) and CPLEX optimize, is constructed to improve the performance of this system in economy, energy and environment. The simulation results indicate that the proposed system is economic in investment and performs well in reducing pollutant emission as well as saving energy. Results also show that the photovoltaic has better performance in economy than CSP when large capacity energy storage equipment is needed.

articleTitle: Bending Strain Comparison on Various Spacer Damper Arms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Wind-induced conductor motion such as Aeolian vibration and subspan oscillation of bundled conductors can lead to reduced lifespan and need for excessive maintenance of overhead lines if left unaddressed. Extended exposure to significant strain levels can result in damaged and even broken conductor stranding. The highest strain levels in these systems are typically found at the suspension clamp and spacer attachment points. Reduction of strain levels in these locations can promote increase conductor life and more reliable service networks. Test results showed a significant reduction in strain when using an elastomer lined clamp compared to a metal-to-metal clamp.

articleTitle: Electrical Network Equivalent Modeling Method with Boundary Buses Interconnected
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes an equivalent modeling method (EMM) based on system measurements to reduce the scale of electrical network. In this method, the equivalent network model adopts a novel framework with boundary buses interconnected to improve the accuracy of equivalent network while maintaining the simplicity of the network structure. Obtaining the unknown parameters of equivalent network is regarded as a parameter identification problem in EMM, which is actually a least square estimation (LSE). The objective function of this LSE is built upon the predictive errors without the adoption of weight tuning. The LSE is solved using interior-point method and the optimal solution is regraded as identified parameters. Simulation studies on a 5-bus test system and an IEEE 30-bus test system demonstrate the efficiency and the practicability of the EMM under different operation states.

articleTitle: Construction and Selection of Transmission Modes for Renewable Energy of Western China in the Future
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Distribution of renewable energy and load centers in China is geographically reverse. It is very necessary to transfer large amount of electric power in Western China with long-distance transmission technology. Based on distribution characteristics of western resources and the outgoing power flow in the future, a construction method of transmission modes is proposed. According to this method and the development trend of transmission technology, four specific transmission modes, i.e. UHVAC transmission mode, UHVDC transmission mode, DC grid mode and superconducting transmission mode in Western China, are constructed. The advantages and disadvantages of each mode are also presented. After that, a mode selection model based on the analytic hierarchy process is established to select the most likely mode in 2030 and 2050. Finally, through mathematical calculation, the recommended transmission modes for renewable energy of Western China in 2030 and 2050 are proposed.

articleTitle: Boiler/Turbine Parameter Identification that Uses Primary Frequency Control Experiment Results
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Main steam pressure is supposed to be constant in traditional power system simulation software. However, this leads to greater generation output when large sources (like an ultra high voltage transmission line) are lost, which in turn lead to higher system frequency and smaller load shedding amount. In order to get more precise frequency locus, a boiler model should be used in simulation software after large power source is lost. Boiler heat storage coefficient in the model can be got after primary frequency control (PFC) test when a large step signal is used as disturbance (input). Since turbine valves show obvious nonlinear characteristic for large opening changing, appropriate method should be used to eliminate this non-linear characteristic before parameter estimation can be carried out. This paper shows such a method. Field test shows that turbine parameters and the boiler heat storage coefficient can be obtained one after another.

articleTitle: Solar Powered Irrigation Pumps with Optimum Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper presents the technical, financial and agro-economic aspects of solar powered irrigation pumps. The scheme consists of a PV array, followed by a boost converter for tracking the maximum power point and for impedance matching purpose. The output from the boost converter is fed to a three phase inverter and then to an induction motor-pump set. Rate of flow of water is decided by V/f control of induction motor to provide the optimum power output for a particular head. The pump output is controlled in order to set a MPPT tracking at the solar panel output. Few important crops that are grown all over the world are being examined taking into account the evapotranspiration, seepage and percolation losses. Utmost care has been taken so that the overall cost of the system is low by not considering any storage devices.

articleTitle: Estimation of Field Voltage as Unknown Input Without Exciter-PSS Model and Bad Data Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Field voltage E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">fd</sub> is controlled by the automatic voltage regulator (AVR) to maintain terminal voltage. Very often measurement of E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">fd</sub> is required for dynamic monitoring purposes. Estimation of E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">fd</sub> requires information regarding AVR-PSS, which is often not available. Novelty of the method is that E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">fd</sub> may be treated as unknown input associated with high process noise in Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) so that exciter-PSS models are not required. The method depends on terminal measurements of that generator only, making the algorithm completely independent from the other measurements. Accuracy of the method is shown with results simulated in PSS/E.

articleTitle: Reliability and Economic Efficiency in Power System with PV Considering Import Fuel Price Transition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: In conventional power systems, large power sources such as thermal, hydro, and nuclear power plants supply the vast majority of the electricity. However, in future power systems, the installed capacities of renewable energy sources such as wind power and photovoltaic generation (PV) systems will increase, and these sources will supply a large volume of electricity. The potentially frequent occurrence of supply-demand imbalances in future power systems is a concern. Therefore, coordinated operation with supply-demand balancing between large power sources and renewable energy sources is necessary. In this study, we focus on operation with supply-demand balancing and PV generation, considering both economic efficiency and reliability. We evaluate the impact of import fuel price transitions on supply and demand in a future power system (for the assumed period of 2030-2050) in which a large PV generation source is installed. We conducted numerical simulations on a bulk power system model. We consider both the import fuel price and PV-generation installed capacity as parameters.

articleTitle: Looking to the Future: Thailand’s Electric Vehicles and the Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper analyzed environment impact from electric vehicles (EVs) penetration in Thailand. Although considered as an environmental friendly vehicle due to non-fossil fuel consumption, EV charging consumes power produced by fossil-fuel power plants, and could cause indirect environmental impact. Modified Dynamic Programing (MDP) is employed to perform generation scheduling (GS). Generation costs and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions are compared, considering seasonal variation, EV penetration rate and charging schemes, and application of TOU tariff. The results show that EVs could cause higher production cost, average cost and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions. Charging EV during TOU causes lower cost and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> emissions than Non-TOU for all cases. The higher penetration of EVs causes higher cost and emissions. Policy from utilities are required to encourage EV owners to charge their EVs under TOU.

articleTitle: Contribution-based Energy Scheduling of Cooperative Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a new energy management framework for the coordinated control and management of multiple-coupled microgrids. The objective is to encourage inter-microgrid power exchanges, thereby reducing the demand and reliance on conventional grid power. In order to achieve this objective, a contribution based power scheduling scheme is embodied, that regulates the power exchanges between microgrids within a coalition and that with the upstream grid. Microgrids are prioritized based on their current power demands and their previous contributions to the coalition. Through the proposed framework, microgrids are thereby, rewarded with priority in the present time interval, for their contributions to the coalition in the past. Various system intermittencies are modelled using the scenario generation and reduction processes. Eventually, the efficacy of the proposed framework is verified using several case studies and comparative analysis.

articleTitle: Advanced Latent Thermal Energy Storage for Space Cooling in the Tropics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Space cooling under tropical climatic conditions requires large amounts of energy. Ventilation and air conditioning systems should hence be improved for minimal consumption, while taking into account waste heat management and the urban heat island effect. Latent thermal energy storages are a potential solution here. Principles of low exergy, avoiding inefficient low operating temperatures, are merged with time shifting of cooling and optimal waste heat rejection. Results of this case study indicate unique capabilities to support system efficiency and reduce thermal impact in the proximity, while still being economically attractive. Encapsulated salt hydrates are considered as a storage material, since they provide melting enthalpies of around 200 kJ/kg at near-ambient temperature levels.

articleTitle: Program Development on Condition Assessment of Power Transformer in Generating Plant
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The program development for condition assessment of power transformer in generating plant, mainly oil-immersed type and large power transformer, has been proposed by using the scoring and weighting technique. The database setup for technical specification, factory test as well as routine inspection and maintenance such as visual inspection, insulating oil test and electrical test has been developed by using MySQL with PHP and JAVA programing language. The health index of power transformer components as general condition, active part, insulating oil in main tank, insulating oil in OLTC, bushing and surge arrester as well as overall health index of power transformer can be calculated. The obtained health index can be compared in our power transformer fleet in order to determine the proper maintenance tasks and resource allocation.

articleTitle: Small-signal Stability Evaluation of DFIG Wind Farms with On-site Battery Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Standalone battery energy storage systems (BESS) have widely been integrated to wind turbines recently to enhance the power quality and reliability of wind generation systems. This research analyzes the stability of a doubly fed induction generator (DFIG)-type wind turbines with stand alone battery storage using small-signal analysis. For the wind turbine, the induction generator model, grid side converter (GSC) controller, AC dynamics, and rotor side converter (RSC) controller are considered. For the BESS, the AC filters, and BESS controller are considered in the modeling. Eigenvalue analysis is performed to study the sensitivity of parameters of the system and control parameters on the stability of the combined wind turbine+BESS system. MATLAB/Simulink is used to analyze the system and validate the design.

articleTitle: Volt/Var Control with Electric Vehicle Loads in Distribution Network by Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The demand for electricity caused by a growing number of electric vehicles (EV) is expected to increase and potentially alter load profile seen by the distribution network. Therefore, the system operator face a new challenge for Volt/VAr control, which can be economically achieved by a proper dispatch schedule for on-load tap changer at the substation and fixed and switched capacitors at the substation and at some locations along the feeder. The Volt/VAr scheduling problem subject to system operational constraints was solved by a particle swarm optimization and tested with a distribution system with 69 buses. It can be seen from that the system power loss can be minimized while keeping the voltage profile along the feeder within acceptable limits.

articleTitle: Evaluation of DC Link Capacitor for Solar Fed Dual Inverter with Zero Sequence Elimination PWM
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: In an Inverter, the purpose of DC link capacitor is to maintain the stiff DC bus voltage irrespective of the switching disturbance by providing alternative path for the switching ripple current. To design the capacitor for an inverter the expression for the RMS current ripple at DC link need be computed based on the switching algorithm and load connected with the inverter. In this work, the capacitor requirement for the dual two level inverter configuration operated with zero sequence voltage elimination algorithm is evaluated as in this algorithm full DC bus voltage would appear across the AC phase terminals resulting high dv/dt across AC terminals. The current ripple due to dv/dt is computed in this work by considering the AC current flows through load is pure sinusoidal. Based on the computed current ripple, the appropriate DC link capacitor is identified to maintain the stiff DC bus voltage across the dual inverter configuration. The efficacy of the DC link capacitor computed using theoretical expression is validated through MATLAB simulations. Through the MATLAB simulations it is verified that the current ripple RMS value derived from the theoretical expression is closely matches with the simulation result.

articleTitle: Comparison Approach for Reducing “Demand Response of Consumers” and “Cost of Utility Companies”
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper deals with the comparison approach of operational cost and demand response effort of consumers in a smart grid system. There are two objectives considered for this proposed research i.e. the minimization of the operational cost and labor of consumers for demand responses. Normally, consumers do not want to make much labor (or demand response effort) for reducing or increasing their loads that is why this research is done for reducing consumers toil as well as reducing the cost of generations. Labor of consumers has been considered through the real-time pricing of electricity. Mainly a multi-objective algorithm such as Non-Dominated Sort Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGA-II) has been utilized to determine the optimum Pareto solution. Also, optimal values of NSGA-II has been compared with Epsilon Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm (ε-MOGA. The computer simulation has been performed by the MATLAB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> software.

articleTitle: Case Study: Arc Flash Study of Wang Noi Combined Cycle Power Plant by Handy Arc Flash Calculator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Arc flash is one of the severe electrical hazard which causes injury or decease to workers. EGAT concern about this hazard and develop Handy Arc Flash Calculator (HAFC) used for incident energy calculation according to the IEEE 1584 standard which released on 2002. This document shows a case study of using HAFC compared to ETAP software for Wang Noi Combined Cycle 4 (WNCC4). The results of both methods are the same.Moreover, the warning label which suitable for Thailand is created for the awareness of worker and selection of proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) level.

articleTitle: Development of an Approach to Verify, Calculate and Optimise Protection Settings in a DSO Electrical Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The Provincial Electricity Authority (PEA) operates the distribution networks up to 115 kV of all geographical regions in Thailand, except the metropolitan area (Bangkok Nonthaburi and Samut Prakarn). PEA is working together with Chiang Mai University (CMU) on a research study on the topic of "Wide Area Protection and Coordination for the Electrical Grid of PEA". In this project, DIgSILENT GmbH supplied an approach to verify the effectiveness of the existing protection settings and to identify areas where the protection scheme fails.The region considered in this study is located around Bangkok and includes more than 150 protective relays at the 115 kV level. The Protection Audit Tool of the network calculation software PowerFactory was used to develop the setting verification methodology. This tool evaluates the existing settings independently from the applied protection function by running short circuit calculations in sweeps throughout the network. In order to improve identified performance issues in the protection scheme and to optimise the selection of new protection settings for such a large number of protection devices, Python scripts were developed.This paper summarises the approach used, and presents a comparison between the performance of the original and the newly calculated protection settings.

articleTitle: Short-term Wind Power Local Forecast based on Morphological High-frequency Filter and Local-sensitive Hashing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: As wind power becomes an important part of power systems, more accurate forecast is critical to high-efficiency application of wind power. The paper proposes a novel forecast model of MHF-LSH-SVR based on morphological high-frequency filter (MHF) and local-sensitive hashing algorithms (LSH), focusing on short-term wind power forecast. To mitigate the effect of high volatility of the raw wind power time series on forecast, the MHF filter is used to extract the mean trend time series, which indicates the mean tendency. In order to perform local forecast, the mean trend time series is reconstructed into mean trend segments in the higher-dimension phase space. Afterwards, to obtain more accurate forecast result, the LSH algorithm is applied to pick out the similar segments of the forecast mean trend segment, which are then employed to perform local forecast by the algorithm of support vector regression (SVR). Simulation studies are carried out on the raw wind power time series collected from a real wind farm, and the final results demonstrate that the MHF-LSH-SVR model outperforms the models of persistence (Per.), SVR and MHF-SVR in terms of both accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: The Challenges of Integrating DER
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: As the network operators move to more dynamic ways of operation, there will be new solutions which will help to ensure best use is made of flexibility, demand side response, storage and renewable generation at all network levels, helping to support decarbonisation ambitions and delivering an efficient, resilient and future proofed energy system. This paper will consider how increasing capacity of existing assets, introduction of flexible connections and real-time control will increase the hosting capacity and help ensure that distributed energy resources can be added to networks that would otherwise be considered "full" without running the risk of exceeding operational limits. This approach will also be applicable to future networks, and will be illustrated with example case studies.

articleTitle: Minimizing the Impact of IEC 61850 in the New Automation Projects
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This article describes the challenges that the use of IEC 61850 imposes to the different actors that take part in the different stages of the development of substation automation projects and how some of these challenges can be minimized using the appropriate tools.The use of IEC 61850 imposes a hierarchical information model with a data naming that need to be understood in order to accomplish the engineering process. Besides, the data exchange among the different IEDs in the system may be done either using a point to point client-server communication profile or a point to multipoint publisher-subscriber profile. These data exchanges are configured during the engineering stage providing the data needed by the different IEDs: protective relays, HMI (Human Machine Interfaces) or RTU (Remote Terminal Units).This article suggests the use of the descriptive information in the standard file format SCL (System description Configuration Language) to perform this task and explain how the tools can benefit of this feature.

articleTitle: Advanced Online Volt/var(Q) Control System for Optimal Voltage Profile
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The situation, grid integration of variable renewable energy and electricity sector reforming in Japan, will increase uncertainties in power system operation.To handle these uncertainties, this paper introduces the sophisticated voltage and reactive power management technology based on AC-OPF (Optimal Power Flow) using online data, advanced online volt/var(Q) control system (OPENVQ: Optimized Performance Enabling Network for Volt/var(Q)), which can reduce operating expenditure (OPEX) by transmission loss reduction and optimized control of shunt devices and transformer taps, and/or capital expenditure (CAPEX) by optimized management of voltage control assets. Its architecture consists of a security assessment, a look-ahead operational condition predictor, optimal power flow calculation, and scenario analyzer.To validate the performance of OPENVQ system, a simulator has been developed that can handle multi-period operational conditions considering time series. Simulation results based on the TEPCO Power Grid 1500-bus model show that multiple control procedures created by OPENVQ system can optimize the KPIs, and new logic to reduce the number of control of shunt devices and transformer taps for managing grid voltage could be confirmed.Furthermore the feasibility study of OPENVQ system in Thailand has been conducted by NEDO (New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization)'s study scheme in Japan.

articleTitle: Design of Counterpoise Grounding Electrodes Encased with Low Resistivity Material for Transmission Towers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper presents design of counterpoise electrodes encased with earthing enhancing compounds or more effective grounding (MEG) for transmission towers. Approach is based on a full-wave electromagnetic analysis. For counterpoise analysis, the partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) is used. In this paper, we use lightning parameters from IEC 62305 as reference. For normal case, the soil ionization and frequency dependent parameters are ignored. In cases high ground resistivity more than 1000 ohm-meter, grounding of long counterpoise makes the capacitive result, this make electrode impedance lower than resistance. The impulse impedance of the four-leg and eight-leg counterpoise electrode in area which is high ground resistivity of 5000 ohm-meter, grounding impedance cannot be achieved because of the result of effective length. The MEG is encased with the eight-leg grounding electrode impedance can be accomplished.

articleTitle: Dynamic Equivalent Modeling of Induction Motors based on K-means Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: It is unrealistic to establish the model for analyzing dynamic characteristic of each induction motor. In order to ensure that the equivalent induction motor models impose similar impact on the electric system compared with the original induction motors group, the critical slip s<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cr</sub> and the load rate KL of the induction motor were taken as the clustering indicators in this paper. Induction motors group was clustered based on the K-means algorithm to get different cluster numbers. Then the optimal clustering result was obtained by the F statistics. After the clustering, induction motors in different classes were equalized and the accurate dynamic equivalent models were established. The simulation curves were obtained after comparing the established equivalent models with the original models and the classic models in the short circuit fault condition through the example system. The simulation results proved that the method proposed in this paper were reliable.

articleTitle: NEDA – Precursor to Malaysia Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The New Enhanced Dispatched Arrangement (NEDA) marks another significant achievement towards creating an efficient electricity supply industry for Malaysia (MESI). With the overarching objective of reducing the overall generation cost, NEDA introduces greater competition to the existing PPA generators by allowing the non PPA generators to also participate and sell energy to Single Buyer. This paper looks into the NEDA framework and mechanism and how it is designed to enhance efficiency in the generation sector. In doing so, the paper talks about MESI reform journey that leads to the implementation of NEDA. The paper then elaborates on NEDA mechanism and subsequently discusses the issues and challenges surrounding the implementation of NEDA. The paper finally discusses the way forward to make NEDA an attractive scheme and achieves its intended objectives.

articleTitle: Operation Approach for Battery Exchange Stations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EV) are moving forward in the market as a promising technology for low emissions type of transportation. The charging stations and the battery exchange stations (BES) are taking the interest of the research nowadays. In this paper, an operation approach for BES is proposed. The approach decides the performance of the charging, discharging and the replacement energies of the batteries throughout the day taking into consideration the grid price and the customer arrivals. The BES operation problem is formulated as mixed integer nonlinear programming and solved using the general algebraic modeling system. Simulation and results on a small scale battery exchange station demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed operation approach, which aims at maximizing the BES profit.

articleTitle: Demonstrating the System Benefits of a Single Voltage Source Converter Solution in Transmission Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The paper explores how the evolution of power systems has driven development of STATCOM technology and explains the role of STATCOM in the transmission network. Technological improvements in Voltage Source Converter (VSC) technology are leading to the capability to build larger STATCOMs with a single VSC. The paper analyzes the potential value to transmission network operators as a result of recent developments in the industry. A comparison between a single VSC and a dual VSC STATCOM is performed using a realistic transmission planning case to address the discussion taking place in the industry. The results show that a single VSC STATCOM provides value in the form of increased reliability and availability, reduced required maintenance time, simplified operation and a smaller physical footprint, all while achieving the same system performance.

articleTitle: Application of SSVTs for Rural Electrification of Developing Countries in Asia
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The Station Service Voltage Transformer (SSVT) is an inductive voltage transformer which incorporates the design elements of distribution transformers and instrument transformers. The SSVT was primarily designed for the purpose of providing auxiliary voltage to the substation by connecting directly to the high voltage transmission line and providing a low voltage secondary voltage with power ratings up to several hundred kVA. Recently, its applications have been extended beyond that of auxiliary power. This paper reviews the capability of using the SSVT as an integral component of rural electrification in developing areas by acting as a stand-alone mini substation providing power to communities. Typically, electricity is supplied to communities through a substation where the high voltage is stepped down to medium voltage by a power transformer. The medium voltage is then stepped down to low voltage by means of a distribution transformer. With the SSVT, transformation of high voltage to low voltage is accomplished with one transformer. This provides a low cost, small footprint supplies of electricity to developing communities.

articleTitle: Inventory of Bulk Electric System Inverter-Based Resource Performance in North America
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: The North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) has been working collaboratively with industry stakeholders, inverter manufacturers, and inverter controls and modeling experts to analyze grid disturbances involving bulk power system connected solar photovoltaic resources. These analyses have led to disturbance reports as well as Level 2 NERC Alerts for sharing recommended mitigating actions and mandatory data collection. This paper provides an overview of the findings from these NERC Alerts and a status of bulk power system inverter-based resource performance in North America.

articleTitle: The Best Scenario of Connecting the SPP’s Grid/Generators to the Main System to Minimize the Cost Resulted from Energy Loss and Energy Not Supplied
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a solution to find the best scenario of connecting the SPP's grid or isolated generators to the main system in order to minimize the cost resulted from energy loss and energy not supplied. The capacity of distribution lines and the length of connection line are considered as constraints. Two case studies are simulated by applying the IEEE 33-bus test system. The results in two cases show that if the size of load demand and generation capacity of the SPP's grid is closed to that of the main system, there is a tendency that the minimum costs can occur by connecting both system together. Further, having SPP's grid connected to the main system is more beneficial than having only isolated generators to be connected. It is envisaged that the outcome of this paper is a useful indication for the system operators.

articleTitle: Modular Multilevel Converter Operation in Passive Networks under Unbalanced Loads
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Modular multilevel converters (MMCs) have a promising application in passive network supply, such as offshore platforms and remote loads. In these applications, load imbalance is inevitable, and the maximum-allowable voltage ripples and peak arm currents define the operating limits of modular multilevel converters. This paper investigates the impact of circulating current control supplying passive networks in capacitor voltage ripples of sub-modules and peak arm currents under unbalanced load conditions, comparing the effects of three circulating current control methods on internal variables of the MMCs. The efficacy of the circulating current control is validated through real-time digital simulations of an 400 MVA benchmark MMC-based HVDC transmission system.

articleTitle: Design and Specification for NGR installing in MEA Substation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: As an electricity distribution utility in Thailand, Metropolitan Electricity Authority (MEA) realizes the importance of quality and reliability of the distribution system and aims to improve its services. MEA has a plan to change the neutral grounding scheme of power transformers from solid ground to resistance ground via Neutral Grounding Resistance (NGR). This implementation can reduce the magnitude of ground fault short circuit current and the severity of voltage dip. This article provides the detailed information on the NGR design concepts and methodology behind NGR specification determination. The related equipment in power system which has to be replaced due to the change in magnitude of temporary overvoltage and short circuit current are also proposed. Finally, the suitable resistance value of NGR will be installed at substation to reduce short circuit current and maintain line to line voltage about 90% of the nominal voltage during a single line to ground fault. However, this method can only be applicable in case of a single line to ground fault.

articleTitle: Criticality Evaluation of HV Circuit Breakers in Distribution Substations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to find the quantitative criticality of high voltage circuit breakers placed in different positions of bus configurations commonly used in distribution substations. The Successful Path Method (SPM) is applied to assess the changed reliability of a distribution substation when the failure rate of an individual breaker is varied over a probable range due to alterations in the maintenance program. Subsequently, the criticality of each individual breaker is determined from the rate of change in substation reliability with respect to the varied failure rate of the breaker. Afterward, the quantified criticalities of HV breakers resulted from the proposed method are compared and discussed. Moreover, the results can be perfectly used for risk based maintenance planning.

articleTitle: Impulse Impedance Measurements of Lightning Protection Earthings
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE PES GTD Grand International Conference and Exposition Asia (GTD Asia)
abstract: Lightning protection earthing systems should be tested at currents with time parameters similar to those of lightnings. A method and definition of a measured value of impulse impedance are introduced.
